Cloths
klŏthz
n. pl. (pieces of woven fabric; in Exodus, the “cloths of service” made for ministry in the holy place)
Old English clath. The Authorized Version distinguishes cloths, pieces of fabric, from clothes, garments worn — a distinction modern printing often blurs.

Biblical Definition

The phrase is fixed and it is repeated four times, which in Exodus means it matters: “the cloths of service, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office” (Exo 31:10; and again Exo 35:19, 39:1, 39:41). The material is named: “of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made cloths of service, to do service in the holy place” (Exo 39:1). These were not the priest's vestments — those are listed separately in the same breath — but the coverings and wrappings used in the work: the cloths in which the ark, the table, the candlestick, and the altar were wrapped when the camp moved, described in Numbers 4 with the same care. Somebody wove blue, purple, and scarlet for objects that would spend their travelling life inside a covering of badgers' skins where no Israelite would ever see them. The principle is stated in the phrase itself: cloths of service. Their whole purpose was the work, and their beauty was for God's eyes. Much of the labour of the tabernacle was of this kind, and much of the labour of the church still is.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines cloth as a manufacture or stuff of wool or hair, or of cotton, flax, hemp or other vegetable filaments, formed by weaving; and cloths as the plural, pieces of such stuff.

expand to see more

CLOTH, n. A manufacture or stuff of wool or hair, or of cotton, flax, hemp or other vegetable filaments, formed by weaving or intertexture of threads.

2. The covering of a table; usually called table-cloth.

CLOTHS, plu. Pieces of cloth; distinguished from clothes, garments.

Key Scripture

Exo 31:10 — "And the cloths of service, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office,"

Exo 39:41 — "The cloths of service to do service in the holy place, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons' garments, to minister in the priest's office."

Num 4:6 — "And shall put thereon the covering of badgers' skins, and shall spread over it a cloth wholly of blue, and shall put in the staves thereof."

Modern Corruption

Work no one will ever see is now hard to justify, in a culture where the visible portion of a labour has become the only portion that is thought to count.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Cloths are cloths. The point worth pressing is what was done with them. Blue, purple, and scarlet were the costliest dyes in the ancient world; the cloths of service were made of them; and much of that work went straight underneath a covering of badgers' skins to be carried through a wilderness. The congregation saw an ungainly bundle on the shoulders of the Kohathites. God saw blue. Scripture repeatedly commends labour done where only God is watching, and it is the plainest test of whether a work is being done for Him: alms in secret, prayer in the closet with the door shut, fasting with a washed face, and the Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly. A culture organised around visibility finds this nearly impossible to value. Work that cannot be shown is assumed not to have happened; effort that produces no visible artefact is treated as waste; and the temptation in every ministry is to move resources toward the parts of the work that can be seen. The cloths of service are the corrective, and so is Colossians 3:23 — whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew beged (H899), a garment or covering; bigdey hasserad, the cloths of service; tekeleth (H8504), blue, the costliest of the tabernacle dyes.

expand to see more

Hebrew beged (H899) — a garment, a covering, a cloth; the general word for the tabernacle textiles and for clothing; Exodus 31:10, Numbers 4:6.

Hebrew serad (H8278) — plaited or service work; the phrase bigdey hasserad, cloths of service, unique to these four verses; Exodus 31:10, 35:19, 39:1, 39:41.

Hebrew tekeleth (H8504) — blue, a costly dye; the cloth wholly of blue spread over the ark for its journey; Numbers 4:6, Exodus 26:1.

Usage

"“The cloths of service…to minister in the priest's office” — the phrase repeated four times in Exodus."

"“Of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made cloths of service” — the costliest dyes for the unseen work."

"“A cloth wholly of blue” — under the badgers' skins, where only God would see it."
